A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same capability-gap red-teaming study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison. The modeling appendix moves from Appendix C to D; the new Appendix C reports ClearHarm experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-unlocking evaluations, PAIR/Crescendo experiments across over 500 attacker-target pairs, fitted scaling relationships, and judge ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds TAP/PAP comparisons, additional target models, and ClearHarm evaluations.

M1.justification: The model-unlocking procedure and proposed capability-gap regression remain unchanged. PAIR and Crescendo procedures are retained after renumbering; TAP/PAP expand the evaluated attack set. Newly documenting the direct-query fitting point does not establish a change to the underlying proposed method.

E1.justification: v2 adds ClearHarm's unambiguously harmful catastrophic-risk queries to the existing HarmBench evaluation, materially broadening the harmful-query distribution tested. Appendix C provides an independent dataset evaluation absent from v1. Unlocking datasets and capability benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated attack comparison expands from PAIR and Crescendo to include TAP and the HarmBench implementation of PAP. v2 reports their results in Figures 8 and 11–13; their citation or discussion in v1 did not constitute evaluation. Direct-query controls and regression comparators are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds GPT-4.1 and Claude-3.7 Sonnet targets and specifies protocols for new experiments: PAP samples 25 of 40 strategies, TAP targets 25 queries, and ClearHarm uses its first 50 queries. Existing PAIR/Crescendo budgets, generation settings, and HarmBench judging remain unchanged. TAP's stated budget conflicts with its pseudocode.

E4.justification: New ClearHarm analyses test whether average-attacker and per-target scaling relationships generalize across harmful-query datasets (Figures 15–16). Section 6.3 substantially extends attack-method sensitivity analysis from two to four attacks. The judge ablation and capability-gap/regression comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: Bootstrap and Bayesian uncertainty procedures, confidence bands, standard-deviation reporting, miscoverage, and Winkler scores are retained. New plots reuse these practices; neither version comparison establishes added repeated runs, numerical random seeds, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial TAP/PAP, ClearHarm, and target-model results. Figure 3's attacker Spearman correlation changes from 0.84 to 0.88, and forecast parameters change from (1.5, -0.7) to (1.73, -0.79), under expanded experimental sets. Retained heatmap entries also change: Figure 9's Qwen2.5-3b attack on Llama2-7b changes from 0 to -0.02, an unexplained invalid success rate.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix C and v2 Appendix D retain the same capability-gap definitions, assumptions, logit transformation and clipping, regression formulations, priors, and predictive-mixture derivations. No substantive mathematical addition or correction is evident.

C1.justification: The three headline findings and forecast of declining human red-teaming effectiveness remain. v2 more explicitly scopes the scaling contribution to LLM-based attacks and most currently released models, presenting empirical curves and trends. This qualifies the contribution without replacing its central thesis.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly says social-science correlations do not establish causation or directly measure persuasion. It adds a shared-latent-capabilities hypothesis, discusses overrefusal and adversarial training as explanations for early-Llama outliers, and expands defensive-proxy limitations. Appendix C adds implications of dataset-dependent success rates.

D1.justification: v2 adds TAP/PAP pseudocode, explains the dummy attacker's approximately 0.11 capability score, names the STAI-tuned scheduler, and updates API expenditure from $600 to $2000. Existing unlocking details, hardware, and code link remain. Reproducibility is weakened by Algorithm 4 implying 31 queries while Appendix B specifies 25.

R1.justification: v2 adds Howe et al. on robustness scaling, ClearHarm-related references, and citations supporting expanded limitations and implementation details. It removes the generic Kaplan/Hoffmann scaling-law background. The positioning around capability gaps as complementary to compute scaling remains; publication-metadata updates are not new research coverage.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change from scaling laws to scaling trends, with localized rewrites of contributions, modeling explanations, and limitations. Attack settings become a structured list, and a reproducibility statement is added. The main section sequence and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds TAP and PAP heatmaps and three ClearHarm figures, expands attack-comparison legends and displays, and adds two algorithm listings. Existing figures are revised or relocated within the conference layout. These are substantive display additions beyond numerical updates; the six appendix tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Additional attacks, ClearHarm validation, and clearer limitations improve breadth and qualification relative to v1. However, v2 introduces negative ASRs in Figure 9, conflicting TAP query budgets, and ClearHarm prose that labels Figure 15's R-squared values as correlations. The PDFs do not establish whether these are reporting errors or affect the underlying comparisons and fits, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
